ingredients.name: Finely Chopped Tomatoes with Onion and Garlic
ingredients.buy: Finely Chopped Tomatoes with Onion and Garlic

points: Bring a large saucepan of water to the boil with 1/2 tsp salt for the pasta.
Heat a large frying pan on medium-high heat (no oil).
Once hot, add the pork mince and fry until browned, 5-6 mins. Use a spoon to break it up as it cooks, then drain and discard any excess fat.
Sprinkle over the mixed herbs and cook, stirring, for 1 min more.

notes.text: Wash your hands and equipment after handling raw mince.

steps.title: Fry the Pork

points: Meanwhile, add the linguine to your pan of boiling water and bring back to the boil. Cook until tender, 12 mins.
Once cooked, drain in a colander and pop back in the pan. Drizzle with oil and stir through to stop it sticking together.
steps.title: Cook the Pasta

points: While the pasta cooks, add the Worcester sauce to the pork and allow to bubble away until evaporated, 30 secs.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes, red wine jus paste, sugar and water for the sauce (see pantry for both amounts).
Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat to medium and simmer until the sauce has thickened, 5-6 mins. Add a splash more water if it gets too thick.

notes.text: The mince is cooked when no longer pink in the middle.

steps.title: Make the Sauce

points: When the sauce has thickened, stir in the spinach a handful at a time until wilted and piping hot, 2-3 mins.
steps.title: Add the Spinach

points: Toss the cooked linguine through the sauce along with half the hard Italian style cheese (if it's easier, transfer everything to the pasta saucepan to combine).
Taste and season with salt and pepper if needed. Add a splash of water if the sauce is a little too thick.
steps.title: Combine and Stir

points: Share the porky linguine between your bowls.
Finish with a sprinkle of the remaining hard Italian style cheese.
steps.title: Serve
